notes: Three site-level native signed-lag correlations already exist, but all span both sides of exact matching. Raw annual rows can support one-sided re-extraction where sample size permits.
Nopporo 1999-2017 extends IWE001; useful for directional geometry but not an independent programme.
Bee abundance rises through season while visitation to focal flowers declines; calendar date cannot be treated as one partner-relative window.

Final intact fruit set is available across flowering timing, but the focal Phaulernis window is inferred from oviposition/egg observations and therefore describes realized interaction timing, not independent adult availability.
Strong antagonist-mediated flowering-time selection across 20 populations and two years; partner-relative activity remains unresolved.
Early/late flowering links seed predation and offspring fitness, but the predator window is imported from earlier literature rather than measured contemporaneously.
Early versus late flowering separates pollination and seed-predation consequences in a Hadena system; full extraction must preserve benefit, cost and net channels separately.
Hadena-dominant versus co-pollinator-dominant windows are measured directly and successful fruits are post-predation; quantitative use awaits raw variance verification.
Experimental flowering cohorts are independently ordered by same-season pollinator visitation; final mature seed set is extracted.
2007 early versus middle flowering is ordered by contemporaneous bumble-bee activity and linked to final natural seed set.
Flowering rank and attack demonstrate temporal escape, but realized seed set is model-derived without recoverable variance and cannot serve as final fitness.
Peak and late windows are ordered by measured Centris activity and linked to natural-pollination seed set.
Herbivory timing is experimentally manipulated and viable seed production is measured. This identifies sensitivity to interaction timing but not a natural partner-availability window.

Female butterfly flight is independently measured and plant ramets are followed to dehiscence. The preflight already preserves core-vs-early and core-vs-late separately; numeric 2012-2014 female timing remains the blocker.

Source-reported total-egg and active-egg Gaussian curves show host-stage filtering shifts the effective antagonist peak +0.49 flowering-date SD and narrows sigma from 0.92 to 0.66. This is realized/effective cost geometry, not independent adult-flight timing.

Independent Portuguese Gentiana-Phengaris programme: 127 shoots and 837 eggs show offspring survival varies with host bud size/developmental stage and oviposition period. Replicates host-stage filtering of raw exposure, but does not measure final plant fitness.

Yucca glauca resource allocation makes late distal flowers more likely to abort when basal fruits are present; all Tegeticula eggs in aborted flowers die. Taxonomically distinct host filter; mechanism only, no final plant-fitness effect.

Source Equation 1 propagates the active-egg Gaussian through observed intact-RU fractions and larval survival to final fitness. High-fecundity trough predicts 29.98% loss from baseline; medium predicts 13.72%. Same Cardamine dependence cluster; not independent adult-flight evidence.

Geum urbanum × Byturus ochraceus: predation occurred almost exclusively in the first flowering peak; among predated plants final total seed mass was maximized at an intermediate 36% of flowers in the second peak. This is a realized predator-window/final-fitness tradeoff, not independently censused adult availability.

Ulex europaeus common garden: long-flowering plants escape the seed-predation peak in time, while short-flowering plants fruit during the peak but reduce attack partly via predator satiation. Whole-season infestation is nearly identical (29% vs 30%), and maternal flowering type has no significant effect on annual pod or seed production; retained as a null/boundary against a timing-only escape rule.
